title: Character and Citizenship Education Lessons on Gaza Conflict
what_it_is: Character and Citizenship Education Lessons on Gaza Conflict

sections.label: Teaching Israel-Hamas conflict in schools
sections.summary: Questions ask whether primary students learn about the Israel-Hamas conflict, at which levels, and how content is differentiated by maturity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether primary school students are being taught about the Israel-Hamas conflict, either in the Character and Citizenship Education curriculum or otherwise; (b) if so, at which levels are students taught about the conflict; and (c) how are the contents differentiated among the different levels to take into account the different maturity levels of the students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) with many teachers implementing the Character and Citizenship Education lesson package, how will the Ministry ensure a safe space for students to share diverse views and arrive at their own conclusions on complex issues; and (b) how will the Ministry ensure that students realise the importance of looking at such situations through the lens of Singapore's national interests and the need to maintain our social, racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: CCE slides and safe space
sections.summary: A member cites paragraphs on safe space and religious harmony, and expresses disappointment that the CCE slides were not released.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha may refer to paragraph 36 on how teachers ensure a safe space for discussion of such issues, and paragraphs 28 to 31 and paragraph 51 on the lesson's intent for students to learn how to maintain our religious and racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would like to, first, express deep disappointment that the slides in question, which form the primary teaching resource for the CCE class, have not been released to this House or to the public.

sections.label: Purpose of CCE lessons
sections.summary: The speaker says CCE lessons help students understand emotions, diverse perspectives, verify information, and understand national priorities and interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Indeed, we share his views that this will not be the only sensitive, emotive issue that our students, and even our population, will come across in the days, weeks and years to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is the reason why we feel the importance to conduct the CCE lessons – to help our people understand their emotions, the diversity of perspectives within our society, help our students to learn to verify the information that they come across that is widely available on social media, help them to understand our national priorities, positions and interests.

sections.label: School dialogues and CCE consultations
sections.summary: Questions ask how many schools held dialogue sessions and whether community, religious leaders and teachers were consulted on CCE materials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister let us know, how many schools have organised such dialogue sessions?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And secondly, I understand that the CCE materials were curated with the help of the other agencies, like the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA), can I ask the Minister whether there were any prior consultations, given the context of this issue, with community and religious leaders, as well as prior consultation with the teachers who are to deliver these lessons?

sections.label: Consultation and leadership responsibility
sections.summary: The speaker states consultation does not remove leadership responsibility to decide what is right for society and children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Ultimately, consultation does not take away the leadership responsibility for us to decide what is right and necessary to do for our own society and our children.

sections.label: MOE transparency on CCE materials
sections.summary: MOE says it will show parents the material and explain its use rather than give slides that can be taken out of context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second issue to Mr Leong's question, MOE is being more than transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We are not only prepared to show the parents the material, we are prepared to explain to the parents how the materials are used, rather than to just give a deck of slides which can be taken out of context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, if anything, we are going out of our way to assure parents how we conduct the lessons, rather than just giving a set of slides, as has been proven in the previous episode where people took the slides out of context or took the slides selectively and made comments on it.
